title: Pin-ended column: elastic critical load

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Plane (x-y) problem of the source modelled in 3D with the global Y axis vertical, so that the source's x, y and theta_z are the model's X, Y and rz. In-plane bending is about local z for every member (default orientation), hence the source's I is the section's Iz. Column of 8 m, A = 1.27e4 mm^2, I = 3.66e7 mm^4, E = 200,000 MPa, base pinned, top held laterally. Reference load 1 kN downward at the top; the buckling factor is the critical load in kN. Linear buckling analysis, one member. Target: the theoretical value pi^2 EI/L^2 that the source prints as 1,129 kN. The engine's members carry the exact stability functions (no discretisation error for a prismatic member with constant axial force); the source's computed values use a stated number of elements with a polynomial (approximate) geometric stiffness. The source's two-element value, 1,137 kN, is its own approximation (0.7 % above its theoretical value) and is not a target. Plane stability problem: the source's model has no out-of-plane degrees of freedom. Here the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held and Iy = 1000 Iz, so that no out-of-plane buckling mode precedes the in-plane modes compared; J is a placeholder.

targets.precisionNote: printed "1,129"; tolerance = half a unit in the last printed digit; theoretical value pi^2 EI/L^2 as printed
targets.sign: positive factor on a compressive load
